paper_title: TRIC: A Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator for Electronic Packages

extraction.paper_title: TRIC: A Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator for Electronic Packages

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 4.4, Figure 13 and Table 1 (multi-source eQFN, four HS layouts)
scenario.description: A 9 x 9 mm2 exposed-pad QFN package with a 5 x 5 mm2 epad and a 4 x 4 mm2 die. The die has four 1 x 1 mm2 active areas (heat sources), each dissipating 0.5 W (2 W total, stated as per-source power). Four HS placement layouts (#1-#4) are sketched in Figure 13. The static temperature rise over ambient was computed by TRIC at each HS center (dT1-dT4), at the die center, and as the die maximum. Table 1 reports these in K, for example layout #1 with dTmax = 57.06 K and layout #2 with dTmax = 59.58 K. HS coordinates are only sketched in Figure 13, with no numeric values in the text. No code, repository or data links were found in the packet, so a complete floorplan with x_m, y_m, width_m and height_m for every block cannot be extracted.
scenario.architecture: Exposed-pad QFN (eQFN) package with a multi-source die, modeled as a package-level 3D parametric detailed thermal model (bricks, a board represented as one parallelepiped, and pins represented by an effective-conductivity parallelepiped) and solved with the TRIC projection-based compact thermal model approach. Compared against the FloTHERM finite-volume solver.
scenario.workload: Four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources at 0.5 W each, applied as static (steady-state) power.
scenario.operating_point: Static (steady) conditions, with the temperature rise reported over ambient. The ambient temperature and the exact boundary-condition ambient for this case are not explicitly stated in the paper for this scenario. The paper gives Tamb = 20 C only for the Figure 11 eTQFP cases.

original_setup.solver: TRIC (Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator): a parametric detailed thermal model built from finite-volume bricks on a Cartesian mesh, reduced by a projection-based compact thermal model (CTM) approach with a multigrid iterative solver. Static solution for the multi-source 9 x 9 mm2 eQFN, with a 5 x 5 mm2 epad and a 4 x 4 mm2 die carrying four 1 x 1 mm2 heat sources at 0.5 W each (Section 4.4, Figure 13, Table 1).
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper reports no design or layout optimizer. The random sampling and projection-basis extraction (Algorithms 1-3) are part of the model-order reduction, not a design optimizer. Layouts #1-#4 are compared by hand.
original_setup.controller: None. This scenario is a static thermal analysis with no controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Commercial finite-volume software FloTHERM v12.2. For this multi-source eQFN case the paper says only that the temperature-map maxima agree to within 3%, and the FloTHERM maps are not shown. The paper also gives an overall 15-20x CPU-time reduction for transient impedances.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum over the whole die (dTmax) for layout #1 of the multi-source eQFN. Table 1 also reports dT1-dT4 at the heat-source centers and dTcenter at the die center for layouts #1-#4. The other layouts' dTmax values are 59.58, 55.15 and 56.35 K for layouts #2, #3 and #4.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum of the static temperature-rise field over the die, as computed by TRIC (steady state), over ambient. For layout #1 it equals dT1 = dT2 = dT3 = dT4 = 56.31 K and dTcenter = 57.06 K, so dTmax coincides with dTcenter.

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a full 3D package-level detailed thermal model (die, die attach, epad, mold, leads/pins as an effective-conductivity block, and a board represented as a single parallelepiped). A 2D floorplan-level thermal solver cannot represent the vertical heat paths from die through epad to board, or the board and pin effective conductivities, that set the 57 K rise.

Boundary conditions follow the JEDEC JESD51 junction-to-ambient environment for the package with calibrated heat-transfer coefficients and an assumed board. These package-level and board-level conditions are not specified for this scenario and cannot be mapped onto a generic Studio chip boundary condition without new assumptions.

The solver differs. The paper uses a projection-based compact thermal model derived from a finite-volume detailed model, with a quarter-symmetry reduction for most cases (not for the multi-source analysis, which is excluded). A Studio solver will use a different discretization, so any agreement with the reported 57.06 K would not be an exact replication.
The scenario is steady-state. The paper's transient capability, optimizer and controller play no role, so there are no mismatches in those areas for this scenario.

methods.note: The TRIC description is supported on pp. 2-7: a pDTM solved by finite volumes, a projection-based CTM (Algorithms 1-3), and a FloTHERM v12.2 benchmark with under 3% discrepancy. The 15-20x CPU claim is on pp. 10 and 13. 'No optimizer or controller' and 'static' are consistent with Section 4.4. However, p. 12 does not state the JEDEC ambient or boundary conditions for the multi-source case, and the FloTHERM maps are not shown. Methods are not enough to make the scenario reproducible.

code.note: All 16 pages and the empty assets list show no code, repository, availability statement or input files. Only the DOI and the CC BY license appear. TRIC itself is described as a proprietary graphical tool. Nothing can be verified or executed.

parameters.note: Package size, epad, die, HS size and 0.5 W per HS are verified as text on p. 12. The Table 1 Layout #2 row is garbled in the pdftotext output. The extraction asserts dT4=56.31 and dTcenter=54.13 for layout #2, but the tokens in that garbled row suggest dT4≈54.13 and dTcenter≈57.06. Those cells were not resolved against a rendered table. HS positions, die position, thicknesses, material conductivities, board properties and heat-transfer coefficients are missing. The 375 um die thickness and 0.9 mm package thickness are generic Section 4 or eQFP statements, not stated for this case.

data.note: Table 1 and Figure 13 are only checked via pdftotext, with no rendered page image or asset. The layout #1 row (56.31 x4, 57.06, 57.06) and the layout #3 and #4 rows read consistently. Layout #1 dTmax=57.06 is internally consistent with the paper text that dTcenter=dTmax in layout #1, but it was not confirmed visually. The FloTHERM comparison data for this case is absent.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false). Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power map. The selected scenario is the TRIC multi-source 9x9 mm eQFN (5x5 mm epad, 4x4 mm die, four 1x1 mm sources at 0.5 W each, 2 W total) from Section 4.4, Figure 13 and Table 1. The paper's reported observable is a static die-maximum temperature rise of 57.06 K for layout #1, with 59.58, 55.15 and 56.35 K for layouts #2-#4. Because no Studio result exists, there is nothing to compare against these values, and no numerical agreement or disagreement can be claimed. The requested experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run it would be a steady 2D calculation with no transient trace. The original is a steady 3D package-level model with vertical heat paths through the epad to a board, JEDEC-style boundary conditions and a FloTHERM benchmark (agreement within 3% for maxima). Those essential physical mismatches, together with the missing numeric source coordinates, material properties, board and boundary data, and ambient, mean that even a successful run would support only qualitative sensitivity discussion (for example, how source placement shifts the peak), not a replication. Evidence entries also lack valid page or asset locators, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. No exact replication is claimed.
limitations: Studio did not run (status skipped); no simulated temperature exists and no value can be compared to the paper's 57.06 K.
Feasibility verdict not_2d_applicable; both the input gate and scientific gate failed, so the final verdict and comparison_valid=false are determined by the gate.

The paper's model is a 3D package-level model (die, die attach, epad, mold, pins and board as effective-conductivity blocks) with vertical heat paths that a 2D floorplan solver cannot represent; this essential mismatch also applies to any future 2D run.

Boundary conditions (JEDEC-style environment, heat-transfer coefficients, board) and the ambient temperature for this scenario are not specified, and no mapping onto a generic Studio boundary condition is justified.
Die position, die thickness, die attach and material conductivities are missing or only stated generally for Section 4, so they are not confirmed for this case.
